s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with migration to the right lower quadrant
salient_findings: Abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
Linear lesion within the intestinal lumen on computed tomography
key_facts: Abdominal pain began around the umbilicus 2 days prior
Pain migrated to the right lower quadrant
Air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays
Ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis
Computed tomography showed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Classic presentation of abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings compatible with appendicitis

shortlist.label: Plastron appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound assessment was specifically interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis, which is a type of appendicitis

shortlist.label: Perforated appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays and elevated white-cell count suggest possible perforation

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and imaging findings could also be consistent with Meckel's diverticulitis, a rare but important differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: Linear lesion within the intestinal lumen on computed tomography could represent an intussusception, although it is less likely given the overall clinical picture

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain that migrated to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings compatible with appendicitis, are most consistent with acute appendicitis.

rejected.label: Plastron appendicitis
rejected.why: While the ultrasound assessment was compatible with plastron appendicitis, this term is not a standard medical diagnosis and the overall clinical picture is more consistent with acute appendicitis.

rejected.label: Perforated appendicitis
rejected.why: There is no free air under the diaphragm on plain abdominal X-rays, which makes perforation less likely.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: The location of the pain and the imaging findings are more consistent with appendicitis than Meckel's diverticulitis.

rejected.label: Intussusception
rejected.why: The computed tomography findings of a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen are not typical of intussusception, which usually presents with a target sign or a sausage-shaped mass on imaging.
